briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 31, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴⚠️ Intensification of Global Climate Disasters and Urgent Warnings
sections.content: Recently, climate change-induced disasters have rapidly increased worldwide, sounding serious alarms. In particular, in Nepal, major floods have resulted in numerous missing persons, including 9 South Koreans [18, 40, 41, 42, 58]. This tragedy is assessed as the bill for climate disasters caused by all humanity being pushed onto the most vulnerable regions [43, 51]. Flash floods have also occurred in the Grand Canyon and Indiana, USA, causing casualties and even topographical changes [37, 61], with warming oceans and Himalayan glacier collapses leading to an increase in global disasters [1, 6, 7, 11, 54]. This situation suggests that climate change has already emerged as a 'financial' issue [1, 11], and it is time for the world to heed experts' warnings that we have less time than we think [44, 48].

sections.title: 🇰🇷🌱 Strengthening Domestic Climate Change Response Capabilities and Adaptation Policies
sections.content: Domestically, positive movements to strengthen policy and social response capabilities to climate change are active. A climate adaptation bill has passed the National Assembly, and a 'Climate Crisis Adaptation Map' is scheduled to be created [3], while local governments like Jeongseon County are promoting the establishment of climate change-tailored 'smart farming' and the advancement of agricultural weather observation equipment, thereby enhancing adaptation in the agricultural sector [2, 5]. Furthermore, the Greenhouse Gas Comprehensive Information Center, under the Ministry of Climate, is contributing to international cooperation by inviting greenhouse gas experts from 23 developing countries to Seoul to support the strengthening of their emission calculation and reporting capabilities [9, 10, 14, 15, 16, 17]. Concurrently, efforts to raise public awareness and expand education on the climate crisis are steadily continuing, with young people challenging a 'Climate Suneung' (a climate-themed college entrance exam) [8] and expanded access to climate crisis education for people with disabilities in the Chungnam region [13].

sections.title: 🌱🌍 Accelerating Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition Efforts
sections.content: Domestic and international efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals are also continuously strengthening. Daegu City has generated 1.2 billion KRW in revenue through greenhouse gas reduction [29], and Siheung City is encouraging daily practices through its Carbon Neutrality Point system [27, 31], showcasing ongoing carbon neutrality innovation cases from local governments and public institutions [20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26]. In particular, the domestic renewable energy market is pursuing a six-fold expansion with a target of 220 GW by 2040 [33, 34], and investments and collaborations for energy transition are active, with Korea Western Power entering the Central Asian renewable energy market and SK On supplying large-scale batteries to the US ESS market [35, 38]. However, the news that carbon emission reduction rates in developed countries remained at 0% last year [30] suggests that stronger efforts are needed to achieve global carbon neutrality.

sections.title: 📰🌍 Climate Change Science and Future Outlook
sections.content: Efforts to enhance scientific understanding of climate change and forecast the future are also being pursued concurrently. Recent research suggests that Super El Niño is strengthening, and climate change is intensifying El Niño [46, 50]. Furthermore, the case of 60% forest canopy loss during ancient Earth warming periods [57], along with climate change causing historic garden trees in the UK to 'give up' [49], warns of long-term impacts on ecosystems. Meanwhile, NASA has launched a powerful new space telescope [60, 64], strengthening its observation capabilities for Earth and space environments, which is expected to make significant contributions to climate change research. Alongside the future vision of energy transition, such as the projection that 1.5% of South Korea's land will be utilized for solar power plants by 2040 [36], changes across various industries, including investments in low-carbon steel and clean energy [59], are noteworthy.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of climate disasters and the various domestic and international efforts to overcome them. We encourage your continued interest and action to join in responding to the climate crisis. This concludes the climate briefing for August 31, 2026.
